papers.title: Network-Based Brain Stimulation: Targeting the Frontoparietal Network for Cognitive Rehabilitation After Stroke Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.reason: A human clinical meta-analysis of frontoparietal network stimulation for cognitive rehabilitation after stroke is relevant to neural mechanisms and intervention targets for executive control, though not a computational model.

papers.title: Signatures of Performance Monitoring in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and At-risk Groups: Midfrontal Theta Predicts Divergent Behavioral Adaptation.
papers.reason: This directly studies midfrontal theta and behavioral adaptation in performance monitoring, a core cognitive control mechanism with clear relevance for computational models of executive function.

papers.title: Predictive stability code: Trial-by-trial conflict expectations tune task representations via proactive and reactive spatio-temporo-spectral dynamics
papers.reason: The paper combines trial-by-trial Bayesian conflict-expectancy modelling with EEG representational analyses to explain proactive and reactive cognitive control mechanisms.

papers.title: Toward Closed-Loop Cognitive Modulation in Alzheimer's Disease: BCI-Relevant Evidence and a Translational Roadmap.
papers.reason: This review is relevant to multimodal cognitive-state sensing and adaptive intervention in AD and MCI, but it is broader than executive-function modelling or diagnostic task-based assessment.

papers.title: Females with Epilepsy Show Menstrual Cycle-linked Alterations in Sensory Induced Plasticity
papers.reason: The paper uses EEG and generative modelling in humans, but its focus is sensory plasticity and epilepsy mechanisms rather than executive function, attention, working memory, or planning.

papers.title: Idiosyncratic Random Behavior in a Massive Online Sample
papers.reason: The study models human random sequence generation with a simple computational model, which is relevant to cognitive process modelling but only indirectly tied to executive function constructs.

papers.title: Neurocognitive effects of internal and external attention training in adolescents: insights from Indian yogic practices
papers.reason: The paper reports behavioural and resting-state EEG effects of an attention-focused intervention on attention, executive function, processing speed, and working memory, though it is exploratory and single-arm.

papers.title: Trait Mindfulness and Inhibitory Control in Young Adults: Exploring Sex Moderation and the Potential Mediating Role of Resting-State EEG
papers.reason: The study directly examines inhibitory control using a flanker task, behavioural outcomes, P3 measures, and resting-state EEG, making it clearly relevant to executive control mechanisms.

papers.title: Acute Exercise and Food-Related Cognitive Processing in Adults with Overweight or Obesity: An ERP Study
papers.reason: The paper uses a food-related flanker task and ERP markers of cognitive control, but its main focus is acute exercise and food cue processing with largely null findings.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of the impact of modern antiepileptic drugs on cognitive status and psychoneurological outcomes in patients with post-traumatic epilepsy
papers.reason: The study concerns general cognitive status in post-traumatic epilepsy using MMSE scores, with little specific connection to executive function modelling or digital cognitive biomarkers.

papers.title: Cognitive Impairment After Stroke: Neuroimaging Biomarkers, Artificial Intelligence, and Precision Medicine Approaches
papers.reason: The review covers multimodal biomarkers and AI-based prediction of post-stroke cognitive impairment, but it is broad and not specifically focused on executive function tasks or modelling.
